dymola_subTitle: Physical modeling and simulation tool for model-based design of complex systems
dymola_text: Dymola is a physical modeling and simulation tool that supports model-based design for complex systems. Models are defined based on the Modelica modeling language, providing users with full access to the language. This allows users to freely create their own model libraries or extend existing Modelica libraries to shorten development time, reduce maintenance burdens, and increase model reusability across projects.

An integrated system model can be constructed by combining multi-domain libraries covering various fields such as mechanics, electricity, control, thermal, pneumatics, hydraulics, powertrains, thermodynamics, vehicle dynamics, and air conditioning. Dymola is utilized by companies in various sectors, including automotive, aerospace, architecture, motorsports, energy, and high-tech industries.

Furthermore, Dymola supports the FMI (Functional Mock-up Interface) standard for importing and exporting models, supporting both Model Exchange and Co-Simulation for FMI versions 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0. Real-time simulation is also possible on various HiL (Hardware-in-the-Loop) platforms, enabling testing in environments close to reality.

feat-0.title: Provision of a simulation environment based on the Modelica modeling language
feat-0.text: Dymola is a physical modeling and simulation tool designed based on Modelica, an open standard modeling language. Modelica is an object-oriented, equation-centered language designed to efficiently model complex systems by integrating various physical domains such as mechanics, electricity, hydraulics, thermal, and control. Users can enhance development efficiency and model reusability by directly utilizing the Modelica language or extending existing libraries.

feat-1.title: Support for model exchange and co-simulation based on FMI standards
feat-1.text: Dymola supports both Model Exchange and Co-Simulation based on the FMI (Functional Mock-up Interface) standard. It complies with FMI versions 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0, and allows models to be imported or exported in the FMU (Functional Mock-up Unit) format. Additionally, a Simulink Coder target is provided to compile Simulink models into FMUs, enabling flexible interoperation between various platforms.

feat-2.title: Support for eFMI-based embedded model workflows
feat-2.text: Dymola supports the eFMI (Embedded Functional Mock-up Interface) standard, providing a model-based workflow for embedded system development. eFMI is a standard designed to generate lightweight models and automatically convert them into code optimized for embedded targets. Dymola provides functions to generate models according to the eFMI workflow and export them as C code, which can be effectively utilized for controller design and SIL (Software-in-the-Loop) simulation.

feat-3.title: Support for SSP-based system structure definition and simulation configuration
feat-3.text: Dymola supports the SSP (System Structure and Parameterization) standard, allowing the structure of complex systems to be defined and configured based on XML. SSP provides the ability to hierarchically organize systems containing various FMUs and clearly describe parameter settings and simulation scenarios. Through the function of creating and importing SSP files, Dymola facilitates system-level simulation configuration and collaboration while strengthening interoperability with other tools.

feat-4.title: Adoption of a component-oriented physical modeling approach
feat-4.text: Dymola adopts a component-oriented modeling approach based on the Modelica language, where actual physical parts are represented as objects and combined in a graphical environment using a drag-and-drop method to construct system models. This approach increases model reusability and scalability and supports the intuitive design of complex systems. Furthermore, it improves development productivity by allowing models to be utilized for various analyses without manually reconstructing equations.

feat-5.title: Provision of Modelica application libraries covering various industrial sectors
feat-5.text: Dymola provides Modelica application libraries covering various engineering domains such as hydraulics, mechanics, vehicle dynamics, engines, and architecture. Users can construct system schematics and easily design complex models by utilizing objects representing physical components like valves, resistors, and gears.

feat-6.title: Support for real-time simulation for various HiL platforms
feat-6.text: Dymola supports real-time simulation on various HiL (Hardware-in-the-Loop) platforms such as dSPACE, Concurrent, and xPC. It is compatible with external systems that support Simulink or FMI, and even complex systems like multi-body vehicle dynamics models can be executed in real-time, enabling testing close to the actual environment.

feat-7.title: Provision of a high-performance simulation engine based on symbolic manipulation
feat-7.text: Dymola utilizes symbolic manipulation techniques to solve Differential-Algebraic Equations (DAEs). This method effectively handles problems such as reduced degrees of freedom caused by algebraic loops or constraints, and supports real-time HiL (Hardware-in-the-Loop) simulation through a high-performance numerical solver. This ensures that even complex system models can be executed stably.
